summary.oneLiner: Prozone Realty is strategically monetizing high-performing retail assets in Tier-II cities to redeploy capital into premium Grade-A residential and retail projects in Mumbai's CBD, leveraging peak occupancy and strong footfall to unlock value. The shift from asset-heavy operations to capital-efficient development positions it for margin expansion and higher ROCE in India's most resilient real estate market.

one-line thesis: Prozone Realty is strategically monetizing high-performing retail assets in Tier-II cities to redeploy capital into premium Grade-A residential and retail projects in Mumbai's CBD, leveraging peak occupancy and strong footfall to unlock value. The shift from asset-heavy operations to capital-efficient development positions it for margin expansion and higher ROCE in India's most resilient real estate market.
financial scorecard / credit view: Rs 1,952.2 mn / Rs 939 mn / Rs 178.9 mn / Rs 441.6 mn net debt (FY26); n/a
guidance / outlook: Strategic pivot toward high-yield MMR developments using proceeds from strategic disinvestment of Ch Sambhaji Nagar and Coimbatore malls; targeting premium residential and retail projects in Mumbai CBD.
order book & pipeline: Coimbatore Residential: 402/540 units sold (Rs 2,167 mn); Nagpur Residential: 254/336 units sold (Rs 1,780 mn); Indore Phase 1B: 54/75 plots under EOI
segment / subsidiary detail: Retail: Ch Sambhaji Nagar Mall (94% occupancy, 127 stores, Rs 1,303 mn lease income FY26); Coimbatore Mall (96% occupancy, 113 stores, Rs 1,303 mn lease income FY26). Residential: Coimbatore (540 units, 87+ handed over), Nagpur (336 units, 209 handed over), Indore (Phase 1A: 74 plots completed, Phase 1B: 75 plots under sales)
growth verticals / optionality: Nagpur Mall (0.5m sqft retail + 0.39m sqft development potential); Indore township (43.5 acres, Phase 2+); MMR CBD land acquisition using Rs 1,242.5 Cr disinvestment proceeds
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin: 48.1% (FY26), up from 32.2% (FY25); EBITDA excluding other income margin: 39.3% (FY26); cost control driven by high occupancy and rental stability; no material cost inflation cited
capex / expansion: Rs 1,242.5 Cr proceeds targeted for MMR development capex; no new capex disclosed for existing assets; development capex for Nagpur/Indore already incurred
capital allocation: 100% of Rs 1,242.5 Cr from strategic sale of two malls to be redeployed into premium MMR residential/retail projects; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt reduction not prioritized over growth capex
risks & watch-items: Delays in MMR land acquisition; regulatory approvals for Nagpur Mall; execution risk in residential handovers; LTCG tax impact (12.5% without indexation) on asset sales; reliance on single strategic pivot for future growth
non-obvious takeaways: Despite high occupancy, retail revenue growth is primarily from leasing, not sales; the company is effectively transitioning from a mall operator to a real estate development fund using asset sales as a capital recycling engine

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Deck frames a "Strategic Pivot to MMR": focus toward Grade A Office and Retail platforms in prime Mumbai CBD locations, on the view that "Mumbai has had Infra boom expected to improve realty potential".
- Operating portfolio is two regional malls — Prozone Mall, Ch Sambhaji Nagar and Prozone Mall Coimbatore — which the deck says are "monetized at Peak Performance" and "BOTH PROPERTIES ARE OPERATING AT PEAK OCCUPANCY."
- Development portfolio spans Coimbatore residential, Nagpur residential (with retail), and Indore plotted residential township, i.e. a build-and-sell arm alongside the lease-rental arm.
- Nagpur asset is pitched on catchment: "4.5m catchment population"; Indore is described as a "Prominent business and industrial centre in Madhya Pradesh" with "1.9m city population".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Shareholding] As of Mar 26 the pattern is Promoters 53.56%, FPI 3.05%, Others 43.39% (source: BSE), with named key investors ACACIA Group 3.01%, Radhakishan Damani & Family 0.90% and Sandeep Raheja Group 4.23%.
- [Community/footfall driver] Both malls run a heavy events calendar as footfall drivers — SVEEP voting awareness, Republic Day, Fit India Carnival (SAI), Gudi Padwa and the Ajanta-Ellora International Film Festival at Ch Sambhaji Nagar; Pongal, Women's Day laser & butterfly show, Vookie Eco Fest and a startup gathering at Coimbatore.
